description: `a ?? b` (§7 binary operator; §42 absence): `pick(not)` is the fallback "none", `pick("x")` is "x"; `(@n ?? 0) + 1` reads @n while it is still absent (it is written only after), so @total is 1; the markup `${@n ?? 0}` shows 0 before the click and 4 after. Every `??` here has a left operand that can be `not` where it is read, so no W-NULLISH-NEVER-ABSENT (§42.11 statement 3).
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S440 "all recs on 1-3 and dpa-037" (Gotcha Q2: "`!`, `&&`, `||` (and `and`/`or`) take booleans only; defaults use `??`")
rationale: §7 lists `??` among the binary (infix) operators; §42.8: "`not` … Its runtime representation in compiled JavaScript is `null`" and the absence test matches "both JavaScript `null` and `undefined`" — the values `??` falls through on. S440 Gotcha Q2 makes `??` the default form and Q3 requires a `T | not` operand to be narrowed before arithmetic or a template: `??` is that default, so `(@n ?? 0) + 1` and `${@n ?? 0}` are legal.
